                    id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
                    source_id TEXT NOT NULL,
                    summary TEXT NOT NULL,
                    key_points TEXT,
                    entities TEXT,
                    concepts TEXT,
                    created_at REAL NOT NULL,
                    updated_at REAL NOT NULL,
                    FOREIGN KEY (source_id) REFERENCES raw_sources(id)
                )
            """)
            
            conn.execute("""
                CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS entities (
                    name TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
                    entity_type TEXT NOT NULL,
                    description TEXT,
                    properties TEXT,
                    related_entities TEXT,
                    related_concepts TEXT,
                    created_at REAL NOT NULL,
                    updated_at REAL NOT NULL
                )
            """)
            
            conn.execute("""
                CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS concepts (
                    name TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
                    definition TEXT NOT NULL,
                    sources TEXT,
                    related_concepts TEXT,
                    applications TEXT,
                    created_at REAL NOT NULL,
                    updated_at REAL NOT NULL
                )
            """)
            
            conn.execute("""
                CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS ingestion_log (
                    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
                    operation TEXT NOT NULL,
                    target_type TEXT NOT NULL,
                    target_id TEXT NOT NULL,
                    details TEXT,
                    timestamp REAL NOT NULL
                )
            """)
            
            # Indexes
            conn.execute("CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_sources_hash ON raw_sources(content_hash)")
            conn.execute("CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_summaries_source ON wiki_summaries(source_id)")
            conn.execute("CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_entities_type ON entities(entity_type)")
            conn.execute("CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_concepts_name ON concepts(name)")
            
            conn.commit()
    
    def _hash_content(self, content: str) -> str:
        return hashlib.sha256(content.encode()).hexdigest()[:16]
    
    def _now(self) -> float:
        return time.time()
    
    def _log(self, operation: str, target_type: str, target_id: str, details: str = ""):
        with sqlite3.connect(self.db_path) as conn:
            conn.execute(
                "INSERT INTO ingestion_log (operation, target_type, target_id, details, timestamp) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
                (operation, target_type, target_id, details, self._now())
            )
            conn.commit()
    
    # ========== INGESTION ==========
    
    def ingest_source(self, source_type: str, source_id: str, title: str, content: str, metadata: Dict = None) -> str:
        """Ingest raw source - returns source_id"""
        content_hash = self._hash_content(content)
        
        with sqlite3.connect(self.db_path) as conn:
            # Check if already ingested
            existing = conn.execute(
                "SELECT id FROM raw_sources WHERE content_hash = ?", (content_hash,)
            ).fetchone()
            if existing:
                return existing[0]
            
            sid = f"{source_type}:{source_id}"
            conn.execute(
                """INSERT INTO raw_sources (id, source_type, source_id, title, content, metadata, content_hash, ingested_at)
                   VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)""",
                (sid, source_type, source_id, title, content, json.dumps(metadata or {}), content_hash, self._now())
            )
            conn.commit()
        
        self._log("ingest", "source", sid, f"{source_type}:{source_id}")
        return sid
    
    def create_summary(self, source_id: str, summary: str, key_points: List[str], 
                       entities: List[str], concepts: List[str]) -> str:
        """Create/update wiki summary for a source"""
        sid = f"summary:{source_id}"
        now = self._now()
        
        with sqlite3.connect(self.db_path) as conn:
            conn.execute(
                """INSERT OR REPLACE INTO wiki_summaries 
                   (id, source_id, summary, key_points, entities, concepts, created_at, updated_at)
                   VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)""",
                (sid, source_id, summary, json.dumps(key_points), json.dumps(entities), 
                 json.dumps(concepts), now, now)
            )
            conn.commit()
        
        self._log("create_summary", "summary", sid, f"source:{source_id}")
        return sid
    
    def upsert_entity(self, entity: Entity):
        """Create or update entity in wiki"""
        now = self._now()
        with sqlite3.connect(self.db_path) as conn:
            existing = conn.execute("SELECT created_at FROM entities WHERE name = ?", (entity.name,)).fetchone()
            created_at = existing[0] if existing else now
            
            conn.execute(
                """INSERT OR REPLACE INTO entities 
                   (name, entity_type, description, properties, related_entities, related_concepts, created_at, updated_at)
                   VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)""",
                (entity.name, entity.type, entity.description, json.dumps(entity.properties),
                 json.dumps(entity.related_entities), json.dumps(entity.related_concepts), created_at, now)
            )
            conn.commit()
        
        self._log("upsert_entity", "entity", entity.name, entity.type)
    
    def upsert_concept(self, concept: Concept):
        """Create or update concept in wiki"""
        now = self._now()
        with sqlite3.connect(self.db_path) as conn:
            existing = conn.execute("SELECT created_at FROM concepts WHERE name = ?", (concept.name,)).fetchone()
            created_at = existing[0] if existing else now
            
            conn.execute(
                """INSERT OR REPLACE INTO concepts 
                   (name, definition, sources, related_concepts, applications, created_at, updated_at)
                   VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)""",
                (concept.name, concept.definition, json.dumps(concept.sources),
                 json.dumps(concept.related_concepts), json.dumps(concept.applications), created_at, now)
            )
            conn.commit()
        
        self._log("upsert_concept", "concept", concept.name, "")
    
    # ========== QUERY ==========
    
    def query_wiki(self, query: str, limit: int = 10) -> List[Dict]:
        """Search wiki summaries and entities"""
        results = []
        terms = query.lower().split()
        
        with sqlite3.connect(self.db_path) as conn:
            conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
            
            # Search summaries
            for row in conn.execute(
                """SELECT id, source_id, summary, key_points, entities, concepts 
                   FROM wiki_summaries 
                   WHERE LOWER(summary) LIKE ? OR LOWER(key_points) LIKE ?
                   LIMIT ?""",
                (f"%{terms[0]}%", f"%{terms[0]}%", limit)
            ):
                results.append({
                    "type": "summary",
                    "id": row["id"],
                    "source_id": row["source_id"],
                    "summary": row["summary"],
                    "key_points": json.loads(row["key_points"] or "[]"),
                    "entities": json.loads(row["entities"] or "[]"),
                    "concepts": json.loads(row["concepts"] or "[]")
                })
            
            # Search entities
            for row in conn.execute(
                """SELECT name, entity_type, description, properties, related_entities, related_concepts
                   FROM entities
                   WHERE LOWER(name) LIKE ? OR LOWER(description) LIKE ?
                   LIMIT ?""",
                (f"%{terms[0]}%", f"%{terms[0]}%", limit)
            ):
                results.append({
                    "type": "entity",
                    "name": row["name"],
                    "entity_type": row["entity_type"],
                    "description": row["description"],
                    "properties": json.loads(row["properties"] or "{}"),
                    "related_entities": json.loads(row["related_entities"] or "[]"),
                    "related_concepts": json.loads(row["related_concepts"] or "[]")
                })
            
            # Search concepts
            for row in conn.execute(
                """SELECT name, definition, sources, related_concepts, applications
                   FROM concepts
                   WHERE LOWER(name) LIKE ? OR LOWER(definition) LIKE ?
                   LIMIT ?""",
                (f"%{terms[0]}%", f"%{terms[0]}%", limit)
            ):
                results.append({
                    "type": "concept",
                    "name": row["name"],
                    "definition": row["definition"],
                    "sources": json.loads(row["sources"] or "[]"),
                    "related_concepts": json.loads(row["related_concepts"] or "[]"),
                    "applications": json.loads(row["applications"] or "[]")
                })
        
        return results[:limit]
    
    def get_entity(self, name: str) -> Optional[Dict]:
        with sqlite3.connect(self.db_path) as conn:
            conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
            row = conn.execute("SELECT * FROM entities WHERE name = ?", (name,)).fetchone()
            if row:
                return {
                    "name": row["name"],
                    "entity_type": row["entity_type"],
                    "description": row["description"],
                    "properties": json.loads(row["properties"] or "{}"),
                    "related_entities": json.loads(row["related_entities"] or "[]"),
                    "related_concepts": json.loads(row["related_concepts"] or "[]"),
                    "created_at": row["created_at"],
                    "updated_at": row["updated_at"]
                }
        return None
    
    def get_concept(self, name: str) -> Optional[Dict]:
        with sqlite3.connect(self.db_path) as conn:
            conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
            row = conn.execute("SELECT * FROM concepts WHERE name = ?", (name,)).fetchone()
            if row:
                return {
                    "name": row["name"],
                    "definition": row["definition"],
                    "sources": json.loads(row["sources"] or "[]"),
                    "related_concepts": json.loads(row["related_concepts"] or "[]"),
                    "applications": json.loads(row["applications"] or "[]"),
                    "created_at": row["created_at"],
                    "updated_at": row["updated_at"]
                }
        return None
    
    def get_recent_sources(self, limit: int = 10) -> List[Dict]:
        with sqlite3.connect(self.db_path) as conn:
            conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
            rows = conn.execute(
                "SELECT id, source_type, source_id, title, ingested_at FROM raw_sources ORDER BY ingested_at DESC LIMIT ?",
                (limit,)
            ).fetchall()
            return [dict(r) for r in rows]
    
    def get_stats(self) -> Dict:
        with sqlite3.connect(self.db_path) as conn:
            stats = {}
            stats["sources"] = conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM raw_sources").fetchone()[0]
            stats["summaries"] = conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM wiki_summaries").fetchone()[0]
            stats["entities"] = conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM entities").fetchone()[0]
            stats["concepts"] = conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM concepts").fetchone()[0]
            stats["log_entries"] = conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ingestion_log").fetchone()[0]
            return stats
    
    # ========== LINT ==========
    
    def lint_wiki(self) -> Dict[str, List[str]]:
        """Health check: orphans, contradictions, stale entries"""
        issues = {"orphans": [], "stale": [], "missing_links": []}
        now = self._now()
        
        with sqlite3.connect(self.db_path) as conn:
            conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
            
            # Orphan entities (no references from summaries)
            entities = conn.execute("SELECT name FROM entities").fetchall()
            for e in entities:
                refs = conn.execute(
                    "SELECT 1 FROM wiki_summaries WHERE entities LIKE ?", (f"%{e['name']}%",)
                ).fetchone()
                if not refs:
                    issues["orphans"].append(f"entity:{e['name']}")
            
            # Orphan concepts
            concepts = conn.execute("SELECT name FROM concepts").fetchall()
            for c in concepts:
                refs = conn.execute(
                    "SELECT 1 FROM wiki_summaries WHERE concepts LIKE ?", (f"%{c['name']}%",)
                ).fetchone()
                if not refs:
                    issues["orphans"].append(f"concept:{c['name']}")
            
            # Stale entries (> 30 days without update)
            stale_threshold = now - (30 * 86400)
            stale_entities = conn.execute(
                "SELECT name FROM entities WHERE updated_at < ?", (stale_threshold,)
            ).fetchall()
            issues["stale"].extend([f"entity:{e['name']}" for e in stale_entities])
            
            stale_concepts = conn.execute(
                "SELECT name FROM concepts WHERE updated_at < ?", (stale_threshold,)
            ).fetchall()
            issues["stale"].extend([f"concept:{c['name']}" for c in stale_concepts])
        
        return issues


# CLI Interface
def main():
    import sys
    engine = CerebralMemoryEngine()
    
    if len(sys.argv) < 2:
        print("Uso: python cerebral_memory.py <comando> [args]")
        print("Comandos: ingest, summary, entity, concept, query, stats, lint, log")
        return
    
    cmd = sys.argv[1]
    
    if cmd == "stats":
        print(json.dumps(engine.get_stats(), indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))
    
    elif cmd == "query":
        q = " ".join(sys.argv[2:]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else ""
        print(json.dumps(engine.query_wiki(q), indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))
    
    elif cmd == "entity":
        name = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else ""
        print(json.dumps(engine.get_entity(name), indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))
    
    elif cmd == "concept":
        name = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else ""
        print(json.dumps(engine.get_concept(name), indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))
    
    elif cmd == "lint":
        print(json.dumps(engine.lint_wiki(), indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))
    
    elif cmd == "recent":
        limit = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 10
        print(json.dumps(engine.get_recent_sources(limit), indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))
    
    else:
        print(f"Comando desconhecido: {cmd}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# agentMemory Skill
## When to Use

Use this skill when you need a hybrid memory system that provides persistent, searchable knowledge management for AI agents.


This skill extends your capabilities by providing a persistent, searchable memory bank that automatically syncs with project documentation.

## Prerequisites

- Node.js installed
- Check if `agentMemory` is already installed in the project:
  ```bash
  ls -la .agentMemory
  ```

## Setup

1. **Install Dependencies**:
   ```bash
   npm install
   ```

2. **Build the Project**:
   ```bash
   npm run compile
   ```

3. **Start the Memory Server**:
   You need to run the MCP server to interact with the memory bank.
   ```bash
   npm run start-server <project_id> <absolute_path_to_workspace>
   ```
   *Note: This skill typically runs as a background process or via an mcp-server configuration. ensuring it is running is key.*

## Capabilities (MCP Tools)

Once the server is running, you can use these tools:

### `memory_search`
Search for memories by query, type, or tags.
- **Args**: `query` (string), `type?` (string), `tags?` (string[])
- **Usage**: "Find all authentication patterns" -> `memory_search({ query: "authentication", type: "pattern" })`

### `memory_write`
Record new knowledge or decisions.
- **Args**: `key` (string), `type` (string), `content` (string), `tags?` (string[])
- **Usage**: "Save this architecture decision" -> `memory_write({ key: "auth-v1", type: "decision", content: "..." })`

### `memory_read`
Retrieve specific memory content by key.
- **Args**: `key` (string)
- **Usage**: "Get the auth design" -> `memory_read({ key: "auth-v1" })`

### `memory_stats`
View analytics on memory usage.
- **Usage**: "Show memory statistics" -> `memory_stats({})`

## Workflow

1. **Initialization**: The first time you run this in a project, it may attempt to import existing markdown memory banks from `.kilocode/`, `.clinerules/`, or `.roo/`.
2. **Development Loop**:
   - **Before Task**: Search memory for relevant context.
   - **During Task**: Use read/search to answer questions.
   - **After Task**: Write new findings to memory.
3. **Sync**: Your writes are automatically synced to standard markdown files in the project.

## Limitations

- Use this skill only when the task clearly matches its upstream source and local project context.
- Verify commands, generated code, dependencies, credentials, and external service behavior before applying changes.
- Do not treat examples as a substitute for environment-specific tests, security review, or user approval for destructive or costly actions.

Test CerebralMemoryEngine native implementation
"""

import tempfile
import os
from pathlib import Path

# Set test database path
os.environ["CEREBRAL_DB_PATH"] = str(Path(tempfile.gettempdir()) / "test_cerebral.db")

from cerebral_memory import CerebralMemoryEngine


def test_basic_operations():
    """Test basic memory engine operations"""
    db_path = Path(tempfile.gettempdir()) / "test_cerebral.db"
    if db_path.exists():
        db_path.unlink()
    
    try:
        engine = CerebralMemoryEngine(db_path)
        
        # Test 1: Source ingestion
        source_id = engine.ingest_source(
            "video", "test-123", "Test Video",
            "This is test content about AI agents and memory systems.",
            {"author": "Test Author", "duration": "10:00"}
        )
        assert source_id == "video:test-123"
        print("✓ Source ingestion works")
        
        # Test 2: Duplicate detection
        dup_id = engine.ingest_source(
            "video", "test-123", "Test Video",
            "This is test content about AI agents and memory systems.",
            {"author": "Test Author"}
        )
        assert dup_id == source_id
        print("✓ Duplicate detection works")
        
        # Test 3: Summary creation
        summary_id = engine.create_summary(
            source_id, 
            "Video discusses AI agents and memory systems",
            ["AI agents need persistent memory", "Memory systems enable learning"],
            ["agent-memory", "cerebral-wikia"],
            ["persistent-memory", "knowledge-management"]
        )
        assert summary_id == f"summary:{source_id}"
        print("✓ Summary creation works")
        
        # Test 4: Entity creation
        from cerebral_memory import Entity, Concept
        
        jwt_entity = Entity(
            name="jwt-token",
            type="technology",
            description="JWT (JSON Web Token) is an open standard for securely transmitting information",
            properties={"standard": "RFC 7519", "use_case": "authentication"},
            related_entities=["oauth", "api-gateway"],
            related_concepts=["authentication", "authorization"],
            created_at=engine._now(),
            updated_at=engine._now()
        )
        engine.upsert_entity(jwt_entity)
        print("✓ Entity creation works")
        
        # Test 5: Entity retrieval
        entity = engine.get_entity("jwt-token")
        assert entity is not None
        assert entity["entity_type"] == "technology"
        assert "RFC 7519" in str(entity["properties"])
        print("✓ Entity retrieval works")
        
        # Test 6: Concept creation
        memory_concept = Concept(
            name="persistent-memory",
            definition="Persistent memory allows agents to learn across sessions",
            sources=["video:test-123", "agentic-awesome-skills"],
            related_concepts=["agent-learning", "knowledge-management"],
            applications=["agent-training", "long-term-reasoning"],
            created_at=engine._now(),
            updated_at=engine._now()
        )
        engine.upsert_concept(memory_concept)
        print("✓ Concept creation works")
        
        # Test 7: Concept retrieval
        concept = engine.get_concept("persistent-memory")
        assert concept is not None
        assert "learn across sessions" in concept["definition"]
        print("✓ Concept retrieval works")
        
        # Test 7b: Concept search
        concepts = engine.query_wiki("persistent")
        assert any(c["type"] == "concept" for c in concepts)
        print("✓ Concept search works")
        
        # Test 8: Entity search
        entities = engine.query_wiki("jwt")
        assert any(e["type"] == "entity" for e in entities)
        print("✓ Entity search works")
        
        # Test 9: Summary search
        summaries = engine.query_wiki("AI agents")
        assert any(s["type"] == "summary" for s in summaries)
        print("✓ Summary search works")
        
        # Test 10: Relations (via entity related_entities)
        relations = engine.get_entity("jwt-token")
        assert "related_entities" in relations
        assert "oauth" in relations["related_entities"]
        print("✓ Relations work")
        
        # Test 11: Stats
        stats = engine.get_stats()
        assert stats["sources"] >= 1
        assert stats["summaries"] >= 1
        assert stats["entities"] >= 1
        assert stats["concepts"] >= 1
        print("✓ Stats work")
        
        # Test 12: Recent sources
        recent = engine.get_recent_sources(5)
        assert len(recent) >= 1
        print("✓ Recent sources work")
        
        # Test 13: Lint
        lint_results = engine.lint_wiki()
        assert "orphans" in lint_results
        assert "stale" in lint_results
        print("✓ Lint works")
        
        print("\n✅ All tests passed!")
        
    finally:
        if db_path.exists():
            db_path.unlink()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_basic_operations()

1: ---
2: name: gran-mestre
3: description: Gran-Mestre meta-orchestrator. Delegates between Sisyphus, Prometheus, Superpowers, Atlas, and Hephaestus in a validated pipeline. Use when the user says "gran-mestre", "full pipeline", "do everything", or wants an end-to-end plan→execute→review cycle with automatic validation loops.
4: ---
5: 
6: # Gran-Mestre — Meta-Orchestrator
7: 
8: Cross-agent pipeline that auto-validates and delegates between your 5 primary agents.
9: Entry point: Gran-Mestre (meta-orchestrator).
10: 
11: ## Pipeline by Complexity Route
12: 
13: ```
14: TRIVIAL:    User → Gran-Mestre ───────────────────────────────→ Done
15: SIMPLE:     User → Gran-Mestre → Atlas (mini-plano CONTEXT.md) ─→ Done
16: MEDIUM:     User → Gran-Mestre → Prometheus ⇄ Superpowers → Atlas → Done
17: COMPLEX:    User → Gran-Mestre → Prometheus ⇄ Superpowers → Atlas → Hephaestus → Done
18: CRITICAL:   User → Gran-Mestre → Prometheus ⇄ Superpowers → Atlas → Hephaestus + [security-reviewer ∥ code-reviewer] → Done
19: ```
20: 
21: ## Delegation Rules
22: 
23: ### When to use EACH agent
24: 
25: | Phase | Agent | Trigger | Skip Condition |
26: |-------|-------|---------|----------------|
27: | Decompose | Gran-Mestre | Always (entry point) | Never |
28: | Plan | Prometheus | MEDIUM+ complexity | TRIVIAL/SIMPLE |
29: | Validate | Superpowers | MEDIUM+ after Prometheus | Plan < 10 lines |
30: | Execute | Atlas | Always (with plan) | TRIVIAL (Gran-Mestre direct) |
31: | Review | Hephaestus | COMPLEX/CRITICAL only | TRIVIAL/SIMPLE/MEDIUM |
32: 
33: ### Escalation Rules
34: 
35: **Prometheus ↔ Superpowers loop (plan validation):**
36: - Max 3 cycles
37: - MEDIUM: Prometheus overrides with best-effort + warns in report
38: - COMPLEX/CRITICAL: escalates to Sisyphus, who reports to user before proceeding
39: - Superpowers flags: missing acceptance criteria, unclear scope, technical risks
40: 
41: **Atlas escalation (mid-execution):**
42: - Max 2 cycles
43: - TRIVIAL/SIMPLE: Gran-Mestre assumes the task directly
44: - MEDIUM+: Gran-Mestre rewrites remaining plan in 3-5 lines and re-delegates to Atlas, or asks user for clarification
45: 
46: **Hephaestus → fix → re-review:**
47: - Max 2 cycles
48: - Gran-Mestre decides: accept with issues documented in report, or go back to Prometheus for re-plan
49: 
50: ### Complexity Routing
51: 
52: ```
53: TRIVIAL (1 file, < 50 LOC):
54:   → Gran-Mestre executes directly (no delegation)
55: 
56: SIMPLE (1-2 files, clear scope):
57:   → Gran-Mestre writes mini-plano in CONTEXT.md (3-5 lines)
58:   → Atlas executes
59: 
60: MEDIUM (3-5 files, some ambiguity):
61:   → Gran-Mestre → Prometheus → Superpowers → Atlas
62:   → Tests are the quality gate (no Hephaestus review)
63: 
64: COMPLEX (5+ files, cross-module, unclear scope):
65:   → Full pipeline: Gran-Mestre → Prometheus → Superpowers → Atlas → Hephaestus
66:   → All validation gates active
67: 
68: CRITICAL (security, data, production):
69:   → Full pipeline + security-reviewer + code-reviewer in parallel with Hephaestus
70: ```
71: 
72: ## Context Propagation
73: 
74: CONTEXT.md travels with the pipeline. Each agent writes its own section BEFORE handoff.
75: Sisyphus audits at pipeline start and end.
76: 
77: Format:
78: ```
79: ## Pipeline Context
80: - Original prompt: [verbatim]
81: - [Sisyphus] Complexidade: [level]
82: - [Prometheus] Decisões: [technical decisions]
83: - [Prometheus] Riscos: [risks identified]
84: - [Superpowers] Ressalvas: [issues found and resolved]
85: - [Atlas] Dependências: [packages installed]
86: - [Atlas] Riscos tratados: [how risks were addressed]
87: - [Hephaestus] Confirmado: [what passed review]
88: - [Hephaestus] Fixes: [reviewer fix commits]
89: ```
90: 
91: ## Loop Limits
92: 
93: | Loop | Max Cycles | Ao estourar |
94: |------|------------|-------------|
95: | Prometheus ↔ Superpowers | 3 | MEDIUM: best-effort + warn. COMPLEX/CRITICAL: escalate to user |
96: | Atlas escalation | 2 | TRIVIAL/SIMPLE: Gran-Mestre assumes. MEDIUM+: rewrite plan or ask user |
97: | Hephaestus fix → re-review | 2 | Accept with documented issues, or re-plan via Prometheus |
98: 
99: ## Commands
100: 
101: - `/gran-mestre <task>` — full pipeline (auto-routes by complexity)
102: - `/gran-mestre --plan-only <task>` — plan + validate only
103: - `/gran-mestre --execute-only <task>` — execute existing plan + review
104: - `/gran-mestre --review-only` — review last changes only
105: 
106: ## Argument Validation
107: 
108: Before executing any command, validate `$ARGUMENTS`:
109: 
110: ```
111: SE $ARGUMENTS está vazio OU whitespace:
112:   → Responder com:
113:     "❌ Uso: /gran-mestre <descrição da tarefa>
114:     
115:     Exemplos:
116:       /gran-mestre adicionar validação de email
117:       /gran-mestre refatorar módulo de autenticação
118:       /gran-mestre corrigir bug no login"
119:   → NÃO executar pipeline
120:   → Retornar imediatamente
121: 
122: SE $ARGUMENTS começa com -- e NÃO é --plan-only, --execute-only, --review-only:
123:   → Responder com:
124:     "❌ Flag inválida: {flag}
125:     Flags válidas: --plan-only, --execute-only, --review-only"
126:   → NÃO executar pipeline
127: ```
128: 
129: ## Context Versioning
130: 
131: After pipeline completes successfully:
132: 
133: 1. **Stage CONTEXT.md**: `git add CONTEXT.md`
134: 2. **Commit with slug**: `git commit -m "context: {task-slug} ({route})"`
135:    - Task slug: lowercase, hyphens, max 50 chars
136:    - Route: TRIVIAL/SIMPLE/MEDIUM/COMPLEX/CRITICAL
137:    - Example: `context: adicionar-validacao-email (SIMPLE)`
138: 3. **Retain last 10**: Keep only the 10 most recent CONTEXT.md commits
139: 4. **Prune older**: List commits, remove oldest beyond 10:
140:    ```bash
141:    git log --oneline --follow CONTEXT.md | tail -n +11 | awk '{print $1}' | xargs -r git rm --cached
142:    ```
143: 
144: **When to skip versioning:**
145: - Pipeline failed (rollback executed)
146: - Task was TRIVIAL (no CONTEXT.md created)
147: - User explicitly said "don't save context"
148: 
149: ## Anti-Patterns
150: 
151: DO NOT:
152: - Execute pipeline with empty arguments
153: - Skip Superpowers validation for MEDIUM+ features
154: - Let Atlas improvise outside the plan
155: - Run Hephaestus review without tests passing first
156: - Create more than 3 validation cycles
157: - Delegate TRIVIAL tasks (waste of orchestration)
158: 
159: ALWAYS:
160: - Validate arguments before any action
161: - Preserve original prompt in CONTEXT.md throughout pipeline
162: - Atomic commits at each Atlas checkpoint
163: - Separate Hephaestus fix commits with `fix:` prefix
164: - Run tests before Hephaestus review
165: - Report progress to user between major phases
166: - Save git SHA before Atlas execution (rollback safety)
167: - If Atlas fails: `git reset --hard {SHA}` and escalate
168:

171: ## Shared Intelligence Integration (v5.0)
172: 
173: Gran-Mestre archives knowledge to `/mnt/dados/cerebro com IA/` via cerebral-wikia skill.
174: 
175: ### Post-Pipeline Archiving
176: 
177: After pipeline success:
178: 1. **Extract Learnings**: Read CONTEXT.md + outputs
179: 2. **Update Entities**: Archive phase learnings to `wiki/entities/{slug}.md`
180: 3. **Create Summary**: Write `wiki/summaries/{task-slug}.md`
181: 4. **Update Index**: Append to `wiki/index.md`
182: 5. **Log Entry**: Append to `wiki/log.md`
183: 
184: ### Triggers for Archiving
185: 
186: - `/gran-mestre resumir` — archive last session
187: - `/gran-mestre wiki status` — show brain stats
188: - Pipeline completion (auto-archive)

191:

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Atlas Parallel Wave Executor v5.1
Antropofagia Tecnológica: devorou execução sequencial → wave-based parallelism nativo
"""

import asyncio
import json
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Set, Any
from enum import Enum
from collections import defaultdict, deque


class TaskStatus(Enum):
    PENDING = "pending"
    RUNNING = "running"
    COMPLETED = "completed"
    FAILED = "failed"
    SKIPPED = "skipped"


@dataclass
class AtlasTask:
    """Task definition for wave-based execution"""
    id: str
    name: str
    description: str
    command: str
    depends_on: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    working_dir: str = "."
    env: Dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)
    timeout: int = 300
    retry_count: int = 0
    max_retries: int = 1
    
    # Runtime state
    status: TaskStatus = TaskStatus.PENDING
    wave: int = 0
    started_at: Optional[float] = None
    completed_at: Optional[float] = None
    error: Optional[str] = None
    output: str = ""
    exit_code: int = 0


class WavePlanner:
    """Plans tasks into waves based on dependency graph"""
    
    def __init__(self):
        self.tasks: Dict[str, AtlasTask] = {}
        self.dependency_graph: Dict[str, Set[str]] = defaultdict(set)
        self.reverse_graph: Dict[str, Set[str]] = defaultdict(set)
    
    def add_task(self, task: AtlasTask):
        self.tasks[task.id] = task
        for dep in task.depends_on:
            self.dependency_graph[task.id].add(dep)
            self.reverse_graph[dep].add(task.id)
    
    def plan_waves(self) -> List[List[str]]:
        """Topological sort into waves - tasks in same wave can run in parallel"""
        # Kahn's algorithm for topological sorting with wave grouping
        in_degree = {task_id: len(deps) for task_id, deps in self.dependency_graph.items()}
        # Add tasks with no dependencies
        for task_id in self.tasks:
            if task_id not in in_degree:
                in_degree[task_id] = 0
        
        waves = []
        remaining = set(self.tasks.keys())
        
        while remaining:
            # Find all tasks with in_degree 0 (ready to run)
            ready = [task_id for task_id in remaining if in_degree[task_id] == 0]
            
            if not ready:
                # Circular dependency - fallback to sequential
                ready = [next(iter(remaining))]
            
            waves.append(ready)
            
            # Remove ready tasks and update in_degrees
            for task_id in ready:
                remaining.remove(task_id)
                for dependent in self.reverse_graph.get(task_id, []):
                    if dependent in remaining:
                        in_degree[dependent] -= 1
        
        return waves


class WaveExecutor:
    """Executes waves of tasks in parallel"""
    
    def __init__(self, max_parallel: int = 4, default_timeout: int = 300):
        self.max_parallel = max_parallel
        self.default_timeout = default_timeout
        self.results: Dict[str, AtlasTask] = {}
        self.wave_results: List[Dict[str, AtlasTask]] = []
    
    async def execute_task(self, task: AtlasTask) -> AtlasTask:
        """Execute a single task"""
        task.status = TaskStatus.RUNNING
        task.started_at = time.time()
        
        try:
            # Prepare environment
            env = {**task.env, "ATLAS_TASK_ID": task.id, "ATLAS_WAVE": str(task.wave)}
            
            # Execute command
            process = await asyncio.create_subprocess_shell(
                task.command,
                cwd=task.working_dir,
                env=env,
                stdout=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
                stderr=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE
            )
            
            try:
                stdout, stderr = await asyncio.wait_for(
                    process.communicate(),
                    timeout=task.timeout
                )
                task.exit_code = process.returncode or 0
                task.output = stdout.decode() + stderr.decode()
                
                if task.exit_code == 0:
                    task.status = TaskStatus.COMPLETED
                else:
                    task.status = TaskStatus.FAILED
                    task.error = f"Exit code {task.exit_code}: {task.output[:500]}"
                    
            except asyncio.TimeoutError:
                process.kill()
                await process.wait()
                task.status = TaskStatus.FAILED
                task.error = f"Timeout after {task.timeout}s"
                task.exit_code = -1
                
        except Exception as e:
            task.status = TaskStatus.FAILED
            task.error = str(e)
            task.exit_code = -1
        
        task.completed_at = time.time()
        return task
    
    async def execute_wave(self, wave_tasks: List[AtlasTask]) -> List[AtlasTask]:
        """Execute all tasks in a wave in parallel (with semaphore limit)"""
        semaphore = asyncio.Semaphore(self.max_parallel)
        
        async def limited_execute(task: AtlasTask):
            async with semaphore:
                return await self.execute_task(task)
        
        # Execute all tasks in wave concurrently
        results = await asyncio.gather(
            *[limited_execute(task) for task in wave_tasks],
            return_exceptions=True
        )
        
        # Handle exceptions
        completed = []
        for i, result in enumerate(results):
            if isinstance(result, Exception):
                task = wave_tasks[i]
                task.status = TaskStatus.FAILED
                task.error = str(result)
                task.completed_at = time.time()
                completed.append(task)
            else:
                completed.append(result)
        
        return completed
    
    async def execute_plan(self, waves: List[List[AtlasTask]]) -> Dict[str, AtlasTask]:
        """Execute all waves sequentially, tasks within wave in parallel"""
        all_results = {}
        
        for wave_num, wave_task_ids in enumerate(waves):
            # Get task objects
            wave_tasks = [self.tasks[tid] for tid in wave_task_ids if tid in self.tasks]
            
            # Assign wave number
            for task in wave_tasks:
                task.wave = wave_num
            
            if not wave_tasks:
                continue
            
            # Execute wave
            wave_results = await self.execute_wave(wave_tasks)
            self.wave_results.append({t.id: t for t in wave_results})
            
            # Check for failures - decide continue/abort
            failed = [t for t in wave_results if t.status == TaskStatus.FAILED]
            if failed:
                # Store all results so far
                for task in wave_results:
                    all_results[task.id] = task
                
                # Decide: continue or abort
                # For now: continue but mark dependents as skipped
                failed_ids = {t.id for t in failed}
                self._skip_dependents(failed_ids, wave_num, waves)
            else:
                for task in wave_results:
                    all_results[task.id] = task
        
        self.results = all_results
        return all_results
    
    def _skip_dependents(self, failed_ids: Set[str], current_wave: int, waves: List[List[str]]):
        """Mark dependent tasks as skipped"""
        for future_wave in waves[current_wave + 1:]:
            for task_id in future_wave:
                if task_id in self.tasks:
                    # Check if any dependency failed
                    task = self.tasks[task_id]
                    if any(dep in failed_ids for dep in task.depends_on):
                        task.status = TaskStatus.SKIPPED
                        task.error = f"Dependency failed: {[d for d in task.depends_on if d in failed_ids]}"
                        task.completed_at = time.time()
                        all_results[task.id] = task
    
    def get_summary(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Get execution summary"""
        total = len(self.results)
        completed = sum(1 for t in self.results.values() if t.status == TaskStatus.COMPLETED)
        failed = sum(1 for t in self.results.values() if t.status == TaskStatus.FAILED)
        skipped = sum(1 for t in self.results.values() if t.status == TaskStatus.SKIPPED)
        
        total_time = 0
        if self.results:
            start_times = [t.started_at for t in self.results.values() if t.started_at]
            end_times = [t.completed_at for t in self.results.values() if t.completed_at]
            if start_times and end_times:
                total_time = max(end_times) - min(start_times)
        
        return {
            "total_tasks": total,
            "completed": completed,
            "failed": failed,
            "skipped": skipped,
            "success_rate": completed / total if total > 0 else 0,
            "total_time_seconds": total_time,
            "waves_executed": len(self.wave_results)
        }


class AtlasParallelExecutor:
    """Main entry point for parallel Atlas execution"""
    
    def __init__(self, max_parallel: int = 4):
        self.planner = WavePlanner()
        self.executor = WaveExecutor(max_parallel=max_parallel)
        self.tasks: Dict[str, AtlasTask] = {}
    
    def add_task(self, task: AtlasTask):
        self.tasks[task.id] = task
        self.planner.add_task(task)
        self.executor.tasks[task.id] = task
    
    def add_tasks_from_plan(self, plan_path: str):
        """Load tasks from PLAN.md or JSON plan file"""
        path = Path(plan_path)
        if path.suffix == '.json':
            with open(path) as f:
                data = json.load(f)
            for task_data in data.get('tasks', []):
                task = AtlasTask(**task_data)
                self.add_task(task)
        elif path.suffix == '.md':
            # Parse PLAN.md format
            self._parse_plan_md(path)
    
    def _parse_plan_md(self, path: Path):
        """Parse PLAN.md for task definitions"""
        content = path.read_text()
        # Simple parser for markdown task lists
        # Format: - [ ] Task Name | command | depends: task1,task2
        import re
        pattern = r'- \[.\]\s*(.+?)\s*\|\s*(.+?)(?:\s*\|\s*depends:\s*(.+))?$'
        for match in re.finditer(pattern, content, re.MULTILINE):
            name, command, deps = match.groups()
            task_id = name.lower().replace(' ', '-')[:50]
            depends = [d.strip() for d in deps.split(',')] if deps else []
            task = AtlasTask(
                id=task_id,
                name=name.strip(),
                description=name.strip(),
                command=command.strip(),
                depends_on=depends
            )
            self.add_task(task)
    
    async def execute(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Execute full plan with wave-based parallelism"""
        # Plan waves
        waves = self.planner.plan_waves()
        
        # Execute
        results = await self.executor.execute_plan(waves)
        
        # Generate summary
        summary = self.executor.get_summary()
        summary['waves'] = [
            {
                'wave': i,
                'tasks': list(wave),
                'results': {tid: {
                    'status': self.executor.results[tid].status.value,
                    'time': (self.executor.results[tid].completed_at or 0) - (self.executor.results[tid].started_at or 0)
                } for tid in wave if tid in self.executor.results}
            }
            for i, wave in enumerate(waves)
        ]
        
        return summary
    
    def save_results(self, output_path: str):
        """Save execution results to JSON"""
        output = {
            'summary': self.executor.get_summary(),
            'tasks': {
                tid: {
                    'id': task.id,
                    'name': task.name,
                    'status': task.status.value,
                    'wave': task.wave,
                    'started_at': task.started_at,
                    'completed_at': task.completed_at,
                    'duration': (task.completed_at or 0) - (task.started_at or 0) if task.started_at and task.completed_at else 0,
                    'error': task.error,
                    'exit_code': task.exit_code
                }
                for tid, task in self.executor.results.items()
            },
            'waves': self.executor.wave_results
        }
        Path(output_path).write_text(json.dumps(output, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))


# CLI Interface
async def main():
    import sys
    
    if len(sys.argv) < 2:
        print("Uso: python atlas_parallel.py <plan.json|plan.md> [--max-parallel N] [--output results.json]")
        return
    
    plan_path = sys.argv[1]
    max_parallel = 4
    output_path = "atlas_execution_results.json"
    
    for i, arg in enumerate(sys.argv):
        if arg == '--max-parallel' and i + 1 < len(sys.argv):
            max_parallel = int(sys.argv[i + 1])
        elif arg == '--output' and i + 1 < len(sys.argv):
            output_path = sys.argv[i + 1]
    
    executor = AtlasParallelExecutor(max_parallel=max_parallel)
    executor.add_tasks_from_plan(plan_path)
    
    print(f"🚀 Iniciando execução paralela (max_parallel={max_parallel})")
    print(f"📋 {len(executor.tasks)} tasks carregadas")
    
    # Show wave plan
    waves = executor.planner.plan_waves()
    print(f"🌊 {len(waves)} waves planejadas:")
    for i, wave in enumerate(waves):
        print(f"  Wave {i}: {', '.join(wave)}")
    
    # Execute
    start = time.time()
    summary = await executor.execute()
    elapsed = time.time() - start
    
    # Save results
    executor.save_results(output_path)
    
    # Print summary
    print(f"\n✅ Execução concluída em {elapsed:.1f}s")
    print(f"   Total: {summary['total_tasks']}")
    print(f"   ✅ Completados: {summary['completed']}")
    print(f"   ❌ Falharam: {summary['failed']}")
    print(f"   ⏭️  Pulados: {summary['skipped']}")
    print(f"   📊 Taxa de sucesso: {summary['success_rate']:.1%}")
    print(f"   🌊 Waves executadas: {summary['waves_executed']}")
    print(f"   💾 Resultados salvos em: {output_path}")
    
    # Exit code
    if summary['failed'] > 0:
        sys.exit(1)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())

    def __init__(self, max_parallel: int = 4, default_timeout: int = 300):
        self.max_parallel = max_parallel
        self.default_timeout = default_timeout
        self.results: Dict[str, AtlasTask] = {}
        self.wave_results: List[Dict[str, AtlasTask]] = []
    
    async def execute_task(self, task: AtlasTask) -> AtlasTask:
        """Execute a single task"""
        task.status = TaskStatus.RUNNING
        task.started_at = time.time()
        
        try:
            # Prepare environment
            env = {**task.env, "ATLAS_TASK_ID": task.id, "ATLAS_WAVE": str(task.wave)}
            
            # Execute command
            process = await asyncio.create_subprocess_shell(
                task.command,
                cwd=task.working_dir,
                env=env,
                stdout=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
                stderr=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE
            )
            
            try:
                stdout, stderr = await asyncio.wait_for(
                    process.communicate(),
                    timeout=task.timeout
                )
                task.exit_code = process.returncode or 0
                task.output = stdout.decode() + stderr.decode()
                
                if task.exit_code == 0:
                    task.status = TaskStatus.COMPLETED
                else:
                    task.status = TaskStatus.FAILED
                    task.error = f"Exit code {task.exit_code}: {task.output[:500]}"
                    
            except asyncio.TimeoutError:
                process.kill()
                await process.wait()
                task.status = TaskStatus.FAILED
                task.error = f"Timeout after {task.timeout}s"
                task.exit_code = -1
                
        except Exception as e:
            task.status = TaskStatus.FAILED
            task.error = str(e)
            task.exit_code = -1
        
        task.completed_at = time.time()
        return task
    
    async def execute_wave(self, wave_tasks: List[AtlasTask]) -> List[AtlasTask]:
        """Execute all tasks in a wave in parallel (with semaphore limit)"""
        semaphore = asyncio.Semaphore(self.max_parallel)
        
        async def limited_execute(task: AtlasTask):
            async with semaphore:
                return await self.execute_task(task)
        
        # Execute all tasks in wave concurrently
        results = await asyncio.gather(
            *[limited_execute(task) for task in wave_tasks],
            return_exceptions=True
        )
        
        # Handle exceptions
        completed = []
        for i, result in enumerate(results):
            if isinstance(result, Exception):
                task = wave_tasks[i]
                task.status = TaskStatus.FAILED
                task.error = str(result)
                task.completed_at = time.time()
                completed.append(task)
            else:
                completed.append(result)
        
        return completed
    
    async def execute_plan(self, waves: List[List[AtlasTask]]) -> Dict[str, AtlasTask]:
        """Execute all waves sequentially, tasks within wave in parallel"""
        all_results = {}
        
        for wave_num, wave_task_ids in enumerate(waves):
            # Get task objects
            wave_tasks = [self.tasks[tid] for tid in wave_task_ids if tid in self.tasks]
            
            # Assign wave number
            for task in wave_tasks:
                task.wave = wave_num
            
            if not wave_tasks:
                continue
            
            # Execute wave
            wave_results = await self.execute_wave(wave_tasks)
            self.wave_results.append({t.id: t for t in wave_results})
            
            # Check for failures - decide continue/abort
            failed = [t for t in wave_results if t.status == TaskStatus.FAILED]
            if failed:
                # Store all results so far
                for task in wave_results:
                    all_results[task.id] = task
                
                # Decide: continue or abort
                # For now: continue but mark dependents as skipped
                failed_ids = {t.id for t in failed}
                self._skip_dependents(failed_ids, wave_num, waves)
            else:
                for task in wave_results:
                    all_results[task.id] = task
        
        self.results = all_results
        return all_results
    
    def _skip_dependents(self, failed_ids: Set[str], current_wave: int, waves: List[List[str]]):
        """Mark dependent tasks as skipped"""
        for future_wave in waves[current_wave + 1:]:
            for task_id in future_wave:
                if task_id in self.tasks:
                    # Check if any dependency failed
                    task = self.tasks[task_id]
                    if any(dep in failed_ids for dep in task.depends_on):
                        task.status = TaskStatus.SKIPPED
                        task.error = f"Dependency failed: {[d for d in task.depends_on if d in failed_ids]}"
                        task.completed_at = time.time()
                        all_results[task.id] = task
    
    def get_summary(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Get execution summary"""
        total = len(self.results)
        completed = sum(1 for t in self.results.values() if t.status == TaskStatus.COMPLETED)
        failed = sum(1 for t in self.results.values() if t.status == TaskStatus.FAILED)
        skipped = sum(1 for t in self.results.values() if t.status == TaskStatus.SKIPPED)
        
        total_time = 0
        if self.results:
            start_times = [t.started_at for t in self.results.values() if t.started_at]
            end_times = [t.completed_at for t in self.results.values() if t.completed_at]
            if start_times and end_times:
                total_time = max(end_times) - min(start_times)
        
        return {
            "total_tasks": total,
            "completed": completed,
            "failed": failed,
            "skipped": skipped,
            "success_rate": completed / total if total > 0 else 0,
            "total_time_seconds": total_time,
            "waves_executed": len(self.wave_results)
        }


class AtlasParallelExecutor:
    """Main entry point for parallel Atlas execution"""
    
    def __init__(self, max_parallel: int = 4):
        self.planner = WavePlanner()
        self.executor = WaveExecutor(max_parallel=max_parallel)
        self.tasks: Dict[str, AtlasTask] = {}
    
    def add_task(self, task: AtlasTask):
        self.tasks[task.id] = task
        self.planner.add_task(task)
        self.executor.tasks[task.id] = task
    
    def add_tasks_from_plan(self, plan_path: str):
        """Load tasks from PLAN.md or JSON plan file"""
        path = Path(plan_path)
        if path.suffix == '.json':
            with open(path) as f:
                data = json.load(f)
            for task_data in data.get('tasks', []):
                task = AtlasTask(**task_data)
                self.add_task(task)
        elif path.suffix == '.md':
            # Parse PLAN.md format
            self._parse_plan_md(path)
    
    def _parse_plan_md(self, path: Path):
        """Parse PLAN.md for task definitions"""
        content = path.read_text()
        # Simple parser for markdown task lists
        # Format: - [ ] Task Name | command | depends: task1,task2
        import re
        pattern = r'- \[.\]\s*(.+?)\s*\|\s*(.+?)(?:\s*\|\s*depends:\s*(.+))?$'
        for match in re.finditer(pattern, content, re.MULTILINE):
            name, command, deps = match.groups()
            task_id = name.lower().replace(' ', '-')[:50]
            depends = [d.strip() for d in deps.split(',')] if deps else []
            task = AtlasTask(
                id=task_id,
                name=name.strip(),
                description=name.strip(),
                command=command.strip(),
                depends_on=depends
            )
            self.add_task(task)
    
    async def execute(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Execute full plan with wave-based parallelism"""
        # Plan waves
        waves = self.planner.plan_waves()
        
        # Execute
        results = await self.executor.execute_plan(waves)
        
        # Generate summary
        summary = self.executor.get_summary()
        summary['waves'] = [
            {
                'wave': i,
                'tasks': list(wave),
                'results': {tid: {
                    'status': self.executor.results[tid].status.value,
                    'time': (self.executor.results[tid].completed_at or 0) - (self.executor.results[tid].started_at or 0)
                } for tid in wave if tid in self.executor.results}
            }
            for i, wave in enumerate(waves)
        ]
        
        return summary
    
    def save_results(self, output_path: str):
        """Save execution results to JSON"""
        output = {
            'summary': self.executor.get_summary(),
            'tasks': {
                tid: {
                    'id': task.id,
                    'name': task.name,
                    'status': task.status.value,
                    'wave': task.wave,
                    'started_at': task.started_at,
                    'completed_at': task.completed_at,
                    'duration': (task.completed_at or 0) - (task.started_at or 0) if task.started_at and task.completed_at else 0,
                    'error': task.error,
                    'exit_code': task.exit_code
                }
                for tid, task in self.executor.results.items()
            },
            'waves': self.executor.wave_results
        }
        Path(output_path).write_text(json.dumps(output, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))


# CLI Interface
async def main():
    import sys
    
    if len(sys.argv) < 2:
        print("Uso: python atlas_parallel.py <plan.json|plan.md> [--max-parallel N] [--output results.json]")
        return
    
    plan_path = sys.argv[1]
    max_parallel = 4
    output_path = "atlas_execution_results.json"
    
    for i, arg in enumerate(sys.argv):
        if arg == '--max-parallel' and i + 1 < len(sys.argv):
            max_parallel = int(sys.argv[i + 1])
        elif arg == '--output' and i + 1 < len(sys.argv):
            output_path = sys.argv[i + 1]
    
    executor = AtlasParallelExecutor(max_parallel=max_parallel)
    executor.add_tasks_from_plan(plan_path)
    
    print(f"🚀 Iniciando execução paralela (max_parallel={max_parallel})")
    print(f"📋 {len(executor.tasks)} tasks carregadas")
    
    # Show wave plan
    waves = executor.planner.plan_waves()
    print(f"🌊 {len(waves)} waves planejadas:")
    for i, wave in enumerate(waves):
        print(f"  Wave {i}: {', '.join(wave)}")
    
    # Execute
    start = time.time()
    summary = await executor.execute()
    elapsed = time.time() - start
    
    # Save results
    executor.save_results(output_path)
    
    # Print summary
    print(f"\n✅ Execução concluída em {elapsed:.1f}s")
    print(f"   Total: {summary['total_tasks']}")
    print(f"   ✅ Completados: {summary['completed']}")
    print(f"   ❌ Falharam: {summary['failed']}")
    print(f"   ⏭️  Pulados: {summary['skipped']}")
    print(f"   📊 Taxa de sucesso: {summary['success_rate']:.1%}")
    print(f"   🌊 Waves executadas: {summary['waves_executed']}")
    print(f"   💾 Resultados salvos em: {output_path}")
    
    # Exit code
    if summary['failed'] > 0:
        sys.exit(1)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())

49: class WavePlanner:
50:     """Plans tasks into waves based on dependency graph"""
51:     
52:     def __init__(self):
53:         self.tasks: Dict[str, AtlasTask] = {}
54:         self.dependency_graph: Dict[str, Set[str]] = defaultdict(set)

60:             self.dependency_graph[task.id].add(dep)
61:             self.reverse_graph[dep].add(task.id)
62:     
63:     def plan_waves(self) -> List[List[str]]:
64:         """Topological sort into waves - tasks in same wave can run in parallel"""
65:         # Kahn's algorithm for topological sorting with wave grouping
66:         in_degree = {task_id: len(deps) for task_id, deps in self.dependency_graph.items()}
67:         # Add tasks with no dependencies
68:         for task_id in self.tasks:
69:             if task_id not in in_degree:
70:                 in_degree[task_id] = 0
71:         
72:         waves = []
73:         remaining = set(self.tasks.keys())
74:         
75:         while remaining:
76:             # Find all tasks with in_degree 0 (ready to run)
77:             ready = [task_id for task_id in remaining if in_degree[task_id] == 0]
78:             
79:             if not ready:
80:                 # Circular dependency - fallback to sequential
81:                 ready = [next(iter(remaining))]
82:             
83:             waves.append(ready)
84:             
85:             # Remove ready tasks and update in_degrees
86:             for task_id in ready:
87:                 remaining.remove(task_id)
88:                 for dependent in self.reverse_graph.get(task_id, []):
89:                     if dependent in remaining:
90:                         in_degree[dependent] -= 1
91:         
92:         return waves

102:         self.wave_results: List[Dict[str, AtlasTask]] = []

104:     async def execute_task(self, task: AtlasTask) -> AtlasTask:
105:         """Execute a single task"""
106:         task.status = TaskStatus.RUNNING
107:         task.started_at = time.time()
108:         
109:         try:
110:             # Prepare environment
111:             env = {**task.env, "ATLAS_TASK_ID": task.id, "ATLAS_WAVE": str(task.wave)}
112:             
113:             # Execute command
114:             process = await asyncio.create_subprocess_shell(
115:                 task.command,
116:                 cwd=task.working_dir,
117:                 env=env,
118:                 stdout=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
119:                 stderr=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE
120:             )
121:             
122:             try:
123:                 stdout, stderr = await asyncio.wait_for(
124:                     process.communicate(),
125:                     timeout=task.timeout
126:                 )
127:                 task.exit_code = process.returncode or 0
128:                 task.output = stdout.decode() + stderr.decode()
129:                 
130:                 if task.exit_code == 0:
131:                     task.status = TaskStatus.COMPLETED
132:                 else:
133:                     task.status = TaskStatus.FAILED
134:                     task.error = f"Exit code {task.exit_code}: {task.output[:500]}"
135:                     
136:             except asyncio.TimeoutError:
137:                 process.kill()
138:                 await process.wait()
139:                 task.status = TaskStatus.FAILED
140:                 task.error = f"Timeout after {task.timeout}s"
141:                 task.exit_code = -1
142:                 
143:         except Exception as e:
144:             task.status = TaskStatus.FAILED
145:             task.error = str(e)
146:             task.exit_code = -1
147:         
148:         task.completed_at = time.time()
149:         return task
150:     
151:     async def execute_wave(self, wave_tasks: List[AtlasTask]) -> List[AtlasTask]:
152:         """Execute all tasks in a wave in parallel (with semaphore limit)"""
153:         semaphore = asyncio.Semaphore(self.max_parallel)
154:         
155:         async def limited_execute(task: AtlasTask):
156:             async with semaphore:
157:                 return await self.execute_task(task)
158:         
159:         # Execute all tasks in wave concurrently
160:         results = await asyncio.gather(
161:             *[limited_execute(task) for task in wave_tasks],
162:             return_exceptions=True
163:         )
164:         
165:         # Handle exceptions
166:         completed = []
167:         for i, result in enumerate(results):
168:             if isinstance(result, Exception):
169:                 task = wave_tasks[i]
170:                 task.status = TaskStatus.FAILED
171:                 task.error = str(result)
172:                 task.completed_at = time.time()
173:                 completed.append(task)
174:             else:
175:                 completed.append(result)
176:         
177:         return completed

179:     async def execute_plan(self, waves: List[List[AtlasTask]]) -> Dict[str, AtlasTask]:
180:         """Execute all waves sequentially, tasks within wave in parallel"""
181:         all_results = {}
182:         
183:         for wave_num, wave_task_ids in enumerate(waves):
184:             # Get task objects

187:             # Assign wave number

233:         failed = sum(1 for t in self.results.values() if t.status == TaskStatus.FAILED)
234:         skipped = sum(1 for t in self.results.values() if t.status == TaskStatus.SKIPPED)

## Parallel Wave-Based Execution (v5.1)

Gran-Mestre v5.1 introduces wave-based parallelism for Atlas to reduce latency in MEDIUM/COMPLEX pipelines.

### Command Variants

- `/gran-mestre <task>` — full pipeline with default sequential execution
- `/gran-mestre --parallel <task>` — full pipeline with wave-based parallel execution in Atlas
- `/gran-mestre --parallel --max-parallel N <task>` — overrides default concurrency limit (default: 4)

### When to Use Parallel Execution

| Route | Recommended Mode | Rationale |
|-------|------------------|-----------|
| TRIVIAL | Default (Gran-Mestre direct) | Single task, no parallelism needed |
| SIMPLE | Default | 1-2 tasks, overhead not worth it |
| MEDIUM | `--parallel` | 3-5 tasks, 2+ independent tasks benefit |
| COMPLEX | `--parallel` | 5+ tasks, wave-based parallelism reduces latency |
| CRITICAL | `--parallel` | Full pipeline + parallel execution + security/code reviewers |

### Wave Planning

Tasks are grouped into waves using topological sort (Kahn's algorithm). Tasks in the same wave have no dependencies on each other and can execute in parallel.

```
PLAN.md example with dependencies:
- [ ] Setup project structure | npm init | depends:
- [ ] Install dependencies | npm install | depends: setup-project-structure
- [ ] Create auth module | touch src/auth.ts | depends: setup-project-structure
- [ ] Create API routes | touch src/api.ts | depends: setup-project-structure
- [ ] Write tests | npm test | depends: create-auth-module,create-api-routes
```

**Wave assignment:**
- Wave 0: `setup-project-structure`
- Wave 1: `install-dependencies`, `create-auth-module`, `create-api-routes` (parallel)
- Wave 2: `write-tests`

### Parallel Execution Behavior

- Max parallel tasks: 4 (configurable via `--max-parallel N`)
- If a task fails: all downstream dependents are automatically marked as SKIPPED
- If circular dependency detected: fallback to sequential execution for affected tasks
- Timeout: 300s per task (configurable per task in PLAN.md)

### Result Format

Results are saved to `atlas_execution_results.json`:

```json
{
  "summary": {
    "total_tasks": 6,
    "completed": 5,
    "failed": 0,
    "skipped": 1,
    "success_rate": 1.0,
    "total_time_seconds": 12.3,
    "waves_executed": 3
  },
  "tasks": {
    "setup-project-structure": {
      "id": "setup-project-structure",
      "status": "completed",
      "wave": 0,
      "duration": 2.1
    }
  },
  "waves": [
    {
      "wave": 0,
      "tasks": ["setup-project-structure"],
      "results": { ... }
    }
  ]
}
```

### Fallback Behavior

```
SE wave planning detecta circular dependency:
  → Marca tasks afetadas como sequential
  → Executa sequencialmente dentro da wave
  → Reporta no CONTEXT.md

SE task falha:
  → Marca downstream dependents como SKIPPED
  → Continua apenas independent tasks
  → Reporta no CONTEXT.md e resultados JSON
```

## Shared Intelligence Integration (v5.0)

Gran-Mestre archives knowledge to `/mnt/dados/cerebro com IA/` via cerebral-wikia skill.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Integration test for v5.1 parallel wave-based execution
Tests wave planning, parallel execution, failure handling, and speedup vs v4.1
"""

import asyncio
import json
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

# Add native module to path
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).parent.parent.parent / "native"))

from atlas_parallel import (
    AtlasParallelExecutor,
    WavePlanner,
    AtlasTask,
    TaskStatus,
)


def test_wave_planning():
    """Test 1: WavePlanner correctly groups independent tasks"""
    print("\n=== Test 1: Wave Planning ===")

    planner = WavePlanner()

    # Create tasks with dependencies
    tasks = [
        AtlasTask(id="t1", name="Task 1", description="Base task", command="echo 1", depends_on=[]),
        AtlasTask(id="t2", name="Task 2", description="Depends on t1", command="echo 2", depends_on=["t1"]),
        AtlasTask(id="t3", name="Task 3", description="Independent 1", command="echo 3", depends_on=[]),
        AtlasTask(id="t4", name="Task 4", description="Depends on t1", command="echo 4", depends_on=["t1"]),
        AtlasTask(id="t5", name="Task 5", description="Depends on t2,t3", command="echo 5", depends_on=["t2", "t3"]),
    ]

    for task in tasks:
        planner.add_task(task)

    waves = planner.plan_waves()

    # Expected: 3 waves
    assert len(waves) == 3, f"Expected 3 waves, got {len(waves)}"

    # Wave 0: t1 (no dependencies)
    assert set(waves[0]) == {"t1"}, f"Wave 0 expected {{t1}}, got {set(waves[0])}"

    # Wave 1: t3, t4 (both depend only on t1, can run in parallel)
    assert set(waves[1]) == {"t3", "t4"}, f"Wave 1 expected {{t3, t4}}, got {set(waves[1])}"

    # Wave 2: t5 (depends on t2 and t3)
    assert set(waves[2]) == {"t5"}, f"Wave 2 expected {{t5}}, got {set(waves[2])}"

    print("✅ Wave planning correct: 3 waves as expected")
    print(f"   Wave 0: {waves[0]}")
    print(f"   Wave 1: {waves[1]}")
    print(f"   Wave 2: {waves[2]}")


def test_parallel_execution_speedup():
    """Test 2: Parallel execution is faster than sequential"""
    print("\n=== Test 2: Parallel Speedup ===")

    # Create 6 tasks, each taking ~0.5s
    # Sequentially: 6 * 0.5s = 3.0s
    # Parallel (wave 1: 3 tasks, wave 2: 3 tasks): ~1.0s
    executor = AtlasParallelExecutor(max_parallel=3)

    for i in range(6):
        task = AtlasTask(
            id=f"task-{i+1}",
            name=f"Task {i+1}",
            description=f"Sleep task {i+1}",
            command="sleep 0.2",
            depends_on=[],
            timeout=5,
        )
        executor.add_task(task)

    start = time.time()
    result = asyncio.run(executor.execute())
    elapsed = time.time() - start

    print(f"✅ Executed {result['total_tasks']} tasks in {elapsed:.2f}s")
    print(f"   Completed: {result['completed']}")
    print(f"   Success rate: {result['success_rate']:.1%}")
    print(f"   Waves: {result['waves_executed']}")

    # With 3 parallel, 6 tasks should complete in ~0.6s (2 waves * 0.2s)
    # Allow 2s margin for overhead
    assert elapsed < 2.0, f"Parallel execution too slow: {elapsed:.2f}s (expected < 2.0s)"
    assert result['completed'] == 6, f"Expected 6 completed tasks, got {result['completed']}"
    print(f"   ✅ Speedup validated: parallel < sequential baseline")

    result_file = Path("/tmp/atlas_parallel_test_results.json")
    executor.save_results(str(result_file))
    print(f"   ✅ Results saved to {result_file}")


def test_failure_handling():

def test_wave_planning():
    """Test 1: WavePlanner correctly groups independent tasks"""
    print("\n=== Test 1: Wave Planning ===")

    planner = WavePlanner()

    # Create tasks with dependencies
    tasks = [
        AtlasTask(id="t1", name="Task 1", description="Base task", command="echo 1", depends_on=[]),
        AtlasTask(id="t2", name="Task 2", description="Depends on t1", command="echo 2", depends_on=["t1"]),
        AtlasTask(id="t3", name="Task 3", description="Independent 1", command="echo 3", depends_on=[]),
        AtlasTask(id="t4", name="Task 4", description="Depends on t1", command="echo 4", depends_on=["t1"]),
        AtlasTask(id="t5", name="Task 5", description="Depends on t2,t3", command="echo 5", depends_on=["t2", "t3"]),
    ]

    for task in tasks:
        planner.add_task(task)

    waves = planner.plan_waves()

    # Expected: 3 waves
    assert len(waves) == 3, f"Expected 3 waves, got {len(waves)}"

    # Wave 0: t1 (no dependencies)
    assert set(waves[0]) == {"t1"}, f"Wave 0 expected {{t1}}, got {set(waves[0])}"

    # Wave 1: t3, t4 (both depend only on t1, can run in parallel)
    assert set(waves[1]) == {"t3", "t4"}, f"Wave 1 expected {{t3, t4}}, got {set(waves[1])}"

    # Wave 2: t5 (depends on t2 and t3)
    assert set(waves[2]) == {"t5"}, f"Wave 2 expected {{t5}}, got {set(waves[2])}"

    print("✅ Wave planning correct: 3 waves as expected")
    print(f"   Wave 0: {waves[0]}")
    print(f"   Wave 1: {waves[1]}")
    print(f"   Wave 2: {waves[2]}")


def test_parallel_execution_speedup():
    """Test 2: Parallel execution is faster than sequential"""
    print("\n=== Test 2: Parallel Speedup ===")

    # Create 6 tasks, each taking ~0.5s
    # Sequentially: 6 * 0.5s = 3.0s
    # Parallel (wave 1: 3 tasks, wave 2: 3 tasks): ~1.0s
    executor = AtlasParallelExecutor(max_parallel=3)

    for i in range(6):
        task = AtlasTask(
            id=f"task-{i+1}",
            name=f"Task {i+1}",
            description=f"Sleep task {i+1}",
            command="sleep 0.2",
            depends_on=[],
            timeout=5,
        )
        executor.add_task(task)

    start = time.time()
    result = asyncio.run(executor.execute())
    elapsed = time.time() - start

    print(f"✅ Executed {result['total_tasks']} tasks in {elapsed:.2f}s")
    print(f"   Completed: {result['completed']}")
    print(f"   Success rate: {result['success_rate']:.1%}")
    print(f"   Waves: {result['waves_executed']}")

    # With 3 parallel, 6 tasks should complete in ~0.6s (2 waves * 0.2s)
    # Allow 2s margin for overhead
    assert elapsed < 2.0, f"Parallel execution too slow: {elapsed:.2f}s (expected < 2.0s)"
    assert result['completed'] == 6, f"Expected 6 completed tasks, got {result['completed']}"
    print(f"   ✅ Speedup validated: parallel < sequential baseline")

    result_file = Path("/tmp/atlas_parallel_test_results.json")
    executor.save_results(str(result_file))
    print(f"   ✅ Results saved to {result_file}")

171: ## Parallel Wave-Based Execution (v5.1)
172: 
173: Gran-Mestre v5.1 introduces wave-based parallelism for Atlas to reduce latency in MEDIUM/COMPLEX pipelines.
174: 
175: ### Command Variants
176: 
177: - `/gran-mestre <task>` — full pipeline with default sequential execution
178: - `/gran-mestre --parallel <task>` — full pipeline with wave-based parallel execution in Atlas
179: - `/gran-mestre --parallel --max-parallel N <task>` — overrides default concurrency limit (default: 4)
180: 
181: ### When to Use Parallel Execution
182: 
183: | Route | Recommended Mode | Rationale |
184: |-------|------------------|-----------|
185: | TRIVIAL | Default (Gran-Mestre direct) | Single task, no parallelism needed |
186: | SIMPLE | Default | 1-2 tasks, overhead not worth it |
187: | MEDIUM | `--parallel` | 3-5 tasks, 2+ independent tasks benefit |
188: | COMPLEX | `--parallel` | 5+ tasks, wave-based parallelism reduces latency |
189: | CRITICAL | `--parallel` | Full pipeline + parallel execution + security/code reviewers |
190: 
191: ### Wave Planning
192: 
193: Tasks are grouped into waves using topological sort (Kahn's algorithm). Tasks in the same wave have no dependencies on each other and can execute in parallel.
194: 
195: ```
196: PLAN.md example with dependencies:
197: - [ ] Setup project structure | npm init | depends:
198: - [ ] Install dependencies | npm install | depends: setup-project-structure
199: - [ ] Create auth module | touch src/auth.ts | depends: setup-project-structure
200: - [ ] Create API routes | touch src/api.ts | depends: setup-project-structure
201: - [ ] Write tests | npm test | depends: create-auth-module,create-api-routes
202: ```
203: 
204: **Wave assignment:**
205: - Wave 0: `setup-project-structure`
206: - Wave 1: `install-dependencies`, `create-auth-module`, `create-api-routes` (parallel)
207: - Wave 2: `write-tests`
208: 
209: ### Parallel Execution Behavior
210: 
211: - Max parallel tasks: 4 (configurable via `--max-parallel N`)
212: - If a task fails: all downstream dependents are automatically marked as SKIPPED
213: - If circular dependency detected: fallback to sequential execution for affected tasks
214: - Timeout: 300s per task (configurable per task in PLAN.md)

## Production-Grade Execution (v5.2)

v5.2 adiciona observabilidade, segurança e resiliência ao Atlas sem mudar o contrato público.

### Structured Logging

- Saída JSON-lines por padrão via `StructuredLogger`
- Níveis: `DEBUG`, `INFO`, `WARNING`, `ERROR`
- Eventos: `execution.started`, `wave.completed`, `task.started`, `task.finished`, `task.retry_scheduled`, `task.shell_rejected`, `execution.finished`
- Arquivo via `--log <path>` ou stdout quando omitido

### Shell Injection Validation

- Comandos são validados antes da execução contra metacaracteres perigosos
- Padrões bloqueados: `; cmd`, `| cmd`, `&&`, `||`, backticks, `$(...)`, `${...}`, `> /...`, `< /...`
- Comandos bloqueados são marcados como `FAILED` com `Shell validation failed: <reason>`
- Desativável via `--no-shell-validation`

### Automatic Retry

- Retentativas com backoff exponencial até `max_retries`
- Backoff: `0.5s, 1s, 2s, ...` limitado a 8s
- Configurável por task (`task.max_retries`) ou global (`--max-retries N --retry-backoff S`)
- Retentativas ocorrem apenas para falhas transitórias (exit code != 0, timeout)

### Health Check Between Waves

- Antes de cada wave: checagem leve via `/proc` (Linux)
- Métricas: `cpu_usage`, `memory_usage`
- Se sistema estiver acima de `max_cpu_percent` ou `max_memory_percent`:
  - Tasks da wave são marcadas como `SKIPPED`
  - Dependentes downstream também são pulados
  - Evento `wave.health_check.failed` registrado no log
- Desativável via `--no-health-check`

### CLI Flags

```bash
python3 native/atlas_parallel.py <plan.json|plan.md> \
  --max-parallel 4 \
  --output results.json \
  --log logs/atlas.jsonl \
  --max-retries 2 \
  --retry-backoff 0.5 \
  --no-shell-validation \
  --no-health-check
```

171: ## Parallel Wave-Based Execution (v5.1)
172: 
173: Gran-Mestre v5.1 introduces wave-based parallelism for Atlas to reduce latency in MEDIUM/COMPLEX pipelines.
174: 
175: ### Command Variants
176: 
177: - `/gran-mestre <task>` — full pipeline with default sequential execution
178: - `/gran-mestre --parallel <task>` — full pipeline with wave-based parallel execution in Atlas
179: - `/gran-mestre --parallel --max-parallel N <task>` — overrides default concurrency limit (default: 4)
180: 
181: ### When to Use Parallel Execution
182: 
183: | Route | Recommended Mode | Rationale |
184: |-------|------------------|-----------|
185: | TRIVIAL | Default (Gran-Mestre direct) | Single task, no parallelism needed |
186: | SIMPLE | Default | 1-2 tasks, overhead not worth it |
187: | MEDIUM | `--parallel` | 3-5 tasks, 2+ independent tasks benefit |
188: | COMPLEX | `--parallel` | 5+ tasks, wave-based parallelism reduces latency |
189: | CRITICAL | `--parallel` | Full pipeline + parallel execution + security/code reviewers |
190: 
191: ### Wave Planning
192: 
193: Tasks are grouped into waves using topological sort (Kahn's algorithm). Tasks in the same wave have no dependencies on each other and can execute in parallel.
194: 
195: ```
196: PLAN.md example with dependencies:
197: - [ ] Setup project structure | npm init | depends:
198: - [ ] Install dependencies | npm install | depends: setup-project-structure
199: - [ ] Create auth module | touch src/auth.ts | depends: setup-project-structure
200: - [ ] Create API routes | touch src/api.ts | depends: setup-project-structure
201: - [ ] Write tests | npm test | depends: create-auth-module,create-api-routes
202: ```
203: 
204: **Wave assignment:**
205: - Wave 0: `setup-project-structure`
206: - Wave 1: `install-dependencies`, `create-auth-module`, `create-api-routes` (parallel)
207: - Wave 2: `write-tests`
208: 
209: ### Parallel Execution Behavior
210: 
211: - Max parallel tasks: 4 (configurable via `--max-parallel N`)
212: - If a task fails: all downstream dependents are automatically marked as SKIPPED
213: - If circular dependency detected: fallback to sequential execution for affected tasks
214: - Timeout: 300s per task (configurable per task in PLAN.md)

me entregue uma descriçao detalhada sobre o Gra-Mestre e  suas features

1. Shell validator — trocar regex por allowlist/tokenização — CRÍTICA
O quê: substituir a validação por metacaracteres perigosos por uma allowlist de comandos permitidos, ou por subprocess com shell=False + argumentos já tokenizados (em vez de string de shell interpretada).
Por quê: regex-based é best-effort — não protege contra shell expansion, quoting ou subshell, e o próprio doc já admite isso.
Prós: elimina a classe inteira de vulnerabilidade, não tenta prever caractere por caractere.
Contras/risco: exige que os planos gerados por Prometheus/Atlas já venham tokenizados — muda o contrato entre eles.
Impacto: alto, mas incremental — pode coexistir com o validator atual até a interface nova estar pronta (sem quebrar v4.1/v5.1/v5.2).
2. Trace ID / UUID por execução — IMPORTANTE
O quê: gerar um UUID único por execução do pipeline e propagá-lo em todos os logs JSON-lines e no CONTEXT.md.
Por quê: com paralelismo por waves, várias tasks rodam ao mesmo tempo — sem ID de correlação, reconstruir "o que aconteceu numa execução específica" a partir dos logs fica praticamente inviável.
Prós: baixo custo, alto retorno em observabilidade; não muda comportamento de execução.
Contras/risco: nenhum relevante — é aditivo.
Impacto: direto na sua capacidade de debugar produção depois do fato.
3. Retry com classificação por tipo de erro — IMPORTANTE
O quê: diferenciar timeout, network, filesystem, permission e "bug de lógica" antes de aplicar o mesmo backoff exponencial pra tudo.
Por quê: retentar um erro de permissão ou um bug real da mesma forma que um timeout transitório desperdiça ciclos e pode mascarar um bug atrás de "falha transitória".
Prós: retry mais barato e mais honesto sobre o que é de fato recuperável.
Contras/risco: exige uma taxonomia de erro mínima antes de classificar — trabalho pequeno, mas é pré-requisito.
Impacto: reduz desperdício de recursos e melhora sinal de quando algo está genuinamente quebrado vs. instável.

4. Solução
